methods.label: Find the product of the cube roots
methods.explanation:
Let \(a=\sqrt[3]{x+9}\) and \(b=\sqrt[3]{x-9}\), using real cube roots, which are defined for every real \(x\). Then \(a-b=3\) and \(a^3-b^3=18\). Finding \(ab\) will help because its cube is \((x+9)(x-9)=x^2-81\).

The difference-of-cubes identity connects the known differences:
\[
\begin{aligned}
18&=(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)\\
&=3\bigl((a-b)^2+3ab\bigr)\\
&=27+9ab.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(ab=-1\), and consequently
\[
x^2-81=a^3b^3=(ab)^3=-1.
\]
Therefore \(x^2=80\).

For completeness, the candidates are \(x=\pm4\sqrt5\). For either choice, the corresponding cube roots are
\[
a=\frac{3\pm\sqrt5}{2},\qquad
b=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt5}{2},
\]
with matching signs. Cubing gives \(a^3=9\pm4\sqrt5\) and \(b^3=-9\pm4\sqrt5\), and their difference is \(a-b=3\). Thus both candidates satisfy the original equation. Since \(75<80<85\), the answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
